description: Fire in-app notifications on the important transaction events that currently emit none - most importantly the moment a purchase actually goes through (funds held in escrow). Today the cash-sale flow notifies the seller at 'New purchase request' (initiateCashSale) and 'Payment started' (acceptCashSaleTerms), but when payment SETTLES into ESCROW_HELD - the actual purchase completing - NEITHER buyer nor seller receives any in-app notification. This is the user's reported 'notifications aren't firing on important events like purchasing'. The settlement happens in domain/orchestrator/cashSaleOrchestrator.ts settleCashSale() (reached synchronously via submitClaimedPayment and asynchronously via the CASH_SALE_SETTLE webhook path in lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts). Emit notifications at the correct layer following the existing best-effort createNotification pattern.
steps: Read domain/orchestrator/cashSaleOrchestrator.ts settleCashSale() and submitClaimedPayment(), and lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts CASH_SALE_SETTLE dispatch. Note that the domain orchestrator is a PURE-ish layer that must not import lib/notifications directly (createNotification is 'server-only' and uses the service-role admin client). Decide the emit point: the cleanest options are (a) emit from lib/actions/cashSale.ts after acceptCashSaleTerms when the returned sale.status is ESCROW_HELD/HANDOVER (covers the synchronous Stripe/mock realtime path), AND (b) emit from lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts (or a thin helper it can call) after a successful CASH_SALE_SETTLE (covers the async webhook path). Confirm both paths so a purchase is notified exactly once regardless of how settlement arrives. Guard against double-notify: acceptCashSaleTerms already notifies the seller 'Payment started'; the NEW notification is 'payment cleared / funds held', a distinct event.

Emit a SALE notification to the BUYER on settlement, e.g. title 'Payment confirmed' body 'Your payment is held safely until you receive and approve the item.' link `/purchases` or `/sales/{id}`. Emit a SALE notification to the SELLER, e.g. title 'Funds secured' body 'The buyer has paid. The funds are held in escrow - arrange handover or postage.' link `/sales/{id}`. Do NOT put a currency amount in the body (CashSaleRecord carries no currency field and hardcoding AUD is forbidden - see the existing comment in proposeCashSalePrice).

Wire the webhook settlement path: in lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts after `cashSales.settleCashSale({ cashSaleId })` returns ok, load the buyer_id/seller_id (the admin client is already in scope) and call createNotification for both parties. Keep it best-effort and after the outcome is decided so a notification failure never turns a SUCCESS webhook into a FAILURE (which would make Stripe retry).

Audit the trade flow for the equivalent gap: in lib/actions/trades.ts the collateral-locked / holds-confirmed moment (proposeTrade advancing to COLLATERAL_LOCKED, and the webhook TRADE_EVENT HOLDS_CONFIRMED path) should notify both traders that collateral is locked and the swap is on. Check whether any notification currently fires there; if not, add a best-effort TRADE notification to both traders (use 'trade collateral' / 'card hold' language, NEVER 'escrow' for trades per product.md). If a suitable notification already exists, leave it and record that.

Ensure no duplicate notifications: trace the synchronous path (submitClaimedPayment settles inline and returns to acceptCashSaleTerms) versus the webhook path, and make sure a single logical purchase produces one buyer+one seller settlement notification, not two. The webhook pipeline is idempotent (alreadyProcessed guard) so a re-delivered webhook won't re-notify; the risk is the synchronous path AND a webhook both firing. Prefer emitting the settlement notification from the action layer for the synchronous case and from the webhook only when settlement was NOT already done synchronously (settleCashSale returns INVALID_STATE if already settled - use that to avoid the webhook double-notifying).

Add/extend tests: add unit or component tests asserting that on cash-sale settlement both buyer and seller get a SALE notification, following the fake-repository + spy pattern in tests/unit/cashSaleContract.test.ts and the createNotification usage. If the emit lives in the action/webhook layer, test at that layer (mock createNotification and assert it was called with the right userIds/types). Ensure the trade collateral-locked notification (if newly added) is covered too.
acceptance_criteria: When a cash-sale payment settles (ESCROW_HELD) via the synchronous realtime path, both the buyer and the seller receive exactly one distinct SALE in-app notification about the purchase/funds being held.
When a cash-sale payment settles via the CASH_SALE_SETTLE webhook path, both parties are notified exactly once, and a re-delivered/duplicate webhook does not produce a second notification.
No purchase produces duplicate settlement notifications when both the synchronous and webhook paths could fire.
Trade collateral-locked notification gap is either closed (both traders notified, using card-hold not escrow language) or documented as already covered.
New tests assert the new notification emissions and all previously-passing tests still pass.
No currency amount is embedded in notification bodies; domain purity is preserved (orchestrator does not import server-only notification code).
verification: npm test (new notification tests pass; the ~859 previously-passing tests still pass; the 8 Flutter-agreement failures remain the only failures)
findings:
Added lib/notifications/settlementNotifier.ts with two best-effort helpers that call createNotification (mirrors the existing lib/notifications/payoutNotifier.ts pattern, keeps domain purity - the orchestrator never imports server-only code): notifyCashSaleSettled (SALE notifications to buyer 'Payment confirmed' + seller 'Funds secured', no currency in body, link /sales/{id}) and notifyTradeCollateralLocked (TRADE notifications to both traders, card-hold language, NEVER 'escrow', link /trades/{id}).

CASH-SALE SETTLEMENT (exactly-once across both paths): settlePayment moves PAYMENT_PENDING -> ESCROW_HELD (delivery) or HANDOVER (in-person). Synchronous path: acceptCashSaleTerms in lib/actions/cashSale.ts now branches on the returned sale.status - ESCROW_HELD/HANDOVER means it settled inline (submitClaimedPayment -> settleCashSale for realtime Stripe/mock), so it fires notifyCashSaleSettled to BOTH parties and SKIPS the seller-only 'Payment started' heads-up; PAYMENT_PENDING keeps only 'Payment started' and defers the settlement pair to the webhook. Webhook path: lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts CASH_SALE_SETTLE branch calls notifyCashSaleSettled only when settleCashSale returned ok (result.sale carries buyerId/sellerId). Double-notify is prevented because settleCashSale returns INVALID_STATE (ok:false) if the sale was already settled synchronously, and the pipeline's alreadyProcessed guard stops a redelivered webhook re-dispatching. Emits are best-effort AFTER the outcome is decided, so a notification failure never turns a SUCCESS webhook into a FAILURE.

TRADE COLLATERAL-LOCKED (gap was real - no notification anywhere): added notifyTradeCollateralLocked at every HOLDS_CONFIRMED dispatch site that can reach COLLATERAL_LOCKED, guarded on the applyEvent result state so a self-loop on an already-locked trade emits nothing: lib/actions/trades.ts (proposeTrade zero-bond branch + syncTradeHoldsFromStripe, via shared notifyCollateralLockedIfEntered), lib/trades/collateralPlacement.ts (syncHolds + placeTradeCollateral already-active and zero-bond branches, via shared notifyLockedIfEntered), lib/actions/tradeNegotiation.ts (holds-already-active retry branch), and lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts TRADE_EVENT branch (only when action.tradeEvent === 'HOLDS_CONFIRMED' and result.trade.state === 'COLLATERAL_LOCKED'). Synchronous sync paths and the webhook path are mutually exclusive per trade (realtime vs async provider), mirroring the cash-sale design.

TESTS (12 new, all green): tests/unit/settlementNotifier.test.ts (both-party recipients+types, no currency in body, card-hold not escrow for trades), tests/unit/cashSaleSettleActionNotify.test.ts (action-layer inline ESCROW_HELD/HANDOVER fires settlement pair and NOT 'Payment started'; PAYMENT_PENDING fires only 'Payment started'), tests/unit/settlementWebhookNotify.test.ts (webhook notifies once on ok settle, NOT on INVALID_STATE i.e. already-settled-synchronously, NOT on deduped redelivery; trade collateral notifies on transition into COLLATERAL_LOCKED, not otherwise). Followed the vi.mock pattern from tests/unit/webhookAuthentication.test.ts and the createFakeAdmin fake.

VERIFICATION: npm run typecheck clean. npm run lint unchanged from baseline (1 pre-existing error in scripts/lib/mobileContract.ts + 3 warnings, no new). npm test: 871 passing (was 859 baseline + 12 new), only the 8 pre-existing Flutter-agreement failures remain (mobileDomainAgreement x3, mobileThemeAgreement x5). Note: tests/component/addPaymentMethodDialog.test.tsx emits window.matchMedia uncaught-exception noise (jsdom quirk); verified via git stash that this is pre-existing and unrelated - its 7 assertions pass on the base state too. npm run build not run (documented to fail in-sandbox at /sitemap.xml prerender on missing Supabase env).

REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-16 review, Issue 1 - BLOCKING, cash-sale claim-race double-notify): FIXED. Root cause: acceptCashSaleTerms's claim-race fallback in domain/orchestrator/cashSaleOrchestrator.ts returns { ok: true, sale: current } after reloading an already-settled sale (status ESCROW_HELD/HANDOVER) when claimPayment loses a concurrent race; the action layer branched PURELY on result.sale.status, so a second concurrent/retried accept would re-fire notifyCashSaleSettled for the same purchase. Fix mirrors the webhook's 'did THIS call drive the transition' signal: added an optional `settledNow?: boolean` to the ok variant of CashSaleResult (domain) and CashSaleActionResult (action). settleCashSale is the sole place PAYMENT_PENDING -> ESCROW_HELD/HANDOVER happens, so it now returns settledNow: true; this propagates unchanged through submitClaimedPayment's SETTLED path (return settleCashSale(...)). Every non-settling success path leaves it absent/falsy: the still-PAYMENT_PENDING return ({ ok: true, sale: submitted ?? sale }) and the claim-race fallback ({ ok: true, sale: current }). actionResult in lib/actions/cashSale.ts forwards settledNow, and acceptCashSaleTerms now gates notifyCashSaleSettled on result.settledNow (not status); the seller-only 'Payment started' heads-up now fires on `else if (result.sale.status === 'PAYMENT_PENDING')` so the claim-race fallback (settled sale, no settledNow) emits NOTHING extra. Webhook path unchanged (still keys off settleCashSale returning INVALID_STATE); the 'Payment started' PAYMENT_PENDING behaviour is preserved. Typecheck stays clean (additive optional field).

Regression tests: extended tests/unit/cashSaleSettleActionNotify.test.ts (now 5 tests, +2): existing inline-settle cases updated to carry settledNow: true (genuine settle -> notifyCashSaleSettled fires exactly once, no heads-up); two NEW claim-race cases stub acceptResult as a reloaded ESCROW_HELD (and HANDOVER) sale WITHOUT settledNow and assert notifyCashSaleSettled does NOT fire and no seller heads-up fires; the PAYMENT_PENDING-only heads-up case is unchanged.

RE-VERIFICATION: npm run typecheck clean. npm run lint unchanged from baseline (1 pre-existing error + 3 warnings in scripts/lib/mobileContract.ts and components/trade/ProposeTradeDialog.tsx; no new problems). npm test: 897 passing (895 prior + 2 new), only failures remaining are the 8 pre-existing Flutter-agreement drift checks (mobileDomainAgreement x3, mobileThemeAgreement x5) and the pre-existing addPaymentMethodDialog matchMedia jsdom noise. npm run build not run (documented sitemap prerender failure).

NON-BLOCKING items left as-is per the review's explicit guidance: Issue 2 (typeScaleFloor guard scoped to six files) - NOT expanded codebase-wide; the scoping is a deliberate recorded call and expanding it is out of scope for this fix. The addresses non-transactional demote/promote default and prefillDefault seed-not-overwrite behaviour are accepted as-is (low-impact, and reworking them risks regressing FEAT-003/FEAT-004).
